lesson.title: Design an AI solution
lesson.subtitle: From a real problem to a safe plan

video.title: Design an AI solution
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds, one recurring teacher character. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Dr Farah Rahman — teacher educator from Bangladesh, visiting the school’s AI club (main character)
Mr Okafor — science teacher who runs the school’s AI club (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer, speaking to the student)

chapters.label: A real problem: is AI needed?
Plan for harm, and the lab

scenes.visual: The AI club’s ideas board: one huge sticky note says ‘Build an AI!’ with stars around it. Dr Farah laughs, peels it off and sticks it lower down. In its place she draws a simple person with a question mark beside them.
scenes.animation: The sticky note wobbles as she peels it (200 ms); the person outline draws itself (600 ms).
scenes.narration: Your club’s ideas board says one thing: “Build an AI!” I love the energy. But good designers don’t start with AI. They start with a person who has a problem.

scenes.visual: Paper-grey card. The Darsi mark pops in, then the course name, the lesson title and a yellow ‘AI’ track chip with the spark icon.
scenes.animation: Mark scales 0→100% with a small overshoot (≤ 200 ms); title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: design an AI solution, from a real problem to a safe plan.

scenes.visual: A school office at closing time: a tired secretary, a phone buzzing with a parents’ group chat. The same questions scroll past again and again: exam dates, bus times. A new student and a parent stand at the counter, confused.
scenes.animation: Chat bubbles stack up quickly; two of them get a warning flag.
scenes.narration: Start with a real problem near you, and talk to the people who have it. In a school like yours, the office answers the same questions all day: when are exams, when’s the bus? New students and parents miss the answers in the group chat.

scenes.visual: Two paths. On the left, a tidy notice board by the school gate and a pinned message at the top of the chat, both with a ‘free’ tag. On the right, a phone glowing at 11 at night, with questions typed in three languages and in many different words.
scenes.animation: Left path builds first; the clock on the right ticks to night; the language bubbles pop in.
scenes.on_screen_text: Do you need AI at all?
scenes.narration: Now the hard question: do you need AI at all? A notice board or one pinned message might solve this for free. AI earns its place only when that isn’t enough. Here, questions come late at night, in many words and languages.

scenes.visual: The office secretary hands over a folder: the exam timetable, the bus times, the school rules. A stamp says ‘shared with permission’. A second pile, the class register with names, marks and phone numbers, is pushed away behind a padlock. A magnifying glass moves over the folder only.
scenes.animation: Folder slides across (300 ms); the stamp thumps down; the padlock clicks shut.
scenes.narration: Next, plan the data: where it comes from, with whose permission. Here, it’s the school’s timetable and rules, shared by the office. Nothing personal: no names, marks or phone numbers. And decide what the AI does: search those documents, and answer only from them.

scenes.visual: Clean white card with the AI track chip. Five rows build one by one, each an icon and a question: whose problem, is AI needed, what data, what will the AI do, and what happens when it’s wrong (in red).
scenes.animation: Each row slides in as its question is asked, 300 ms apart.
scenes.on_screen_text: A design plan in five questions
scenes.narration: So, a design plan answers five questions. Whose problem is it? Is AI needed? What data, whose permission, and what will AI do with it? And what happens when it’s wrong?

scenes.visual: A village stream. Children and a woman with a basket wait to cross. Stepping stones appear first; then a simple wooden footbridge with a handrail and a small warning sign. Rain falls; afterwards a person walks along the bridge checking it.
scenes.animation: Stones pop into the water one by one; planks lay themselves across; rain sweeps through, then clears.
scenes.narration: Like building a footbridge over a stream. First, ask who crosses, and when. Maybe stepping stones would do. Then choose strong materials. And plan for floods: a handrail, a sign, someone checking after storms.

scenes.visual: Mr Okafor pops in beside the ideas board, holding the ‘Build an AI!’ note. Three answer cards drop in below him.
scenes.animation: Character slides in from the side; answer cards drop in with a small bounce.
scenes.narration: Quick check! When you design an AI solution, what should come first?

scenes.visual: The card ‘The problem and its people’ gets a check badge. Split screen: on the left, a shiny robot wanders around looking for a job to do; on the right, a student sits with the office secretary, taking notes, and a simple helper takes shape between them.
scenes.animation: Check badge pops (150 ms); the robot shrugs; the helper sketch fills in on the right.
scenes.narration: The problem and its people. Start with the tool, and you’ll hunt for a problem. Start with people, and you’ll build something they actually use.

scenes.visual: Dusk at a bus stop: a student checks the helper on a phone, and the wrong time shows; the bus has already gone. Rewind: now the helper shows the bus timetable as its source, and for an unknown question it says ‘I don’t know, ask the office’. The office secretary ticks a weekly checklist.
scenes.animation: The scene rewinds with a quick scrub; the source card and the ‘I don’t know’ bubble pop in; the checklist ticks.
scenes.narration: Then plan for harm. Who could be hurt by a mistake? A wrong bus time could strand a student after dark. So the helper shows its source, says “I don’t know, ask the office” when nothing matches, and the office checks it weekly. A person stays in charge.

scenes.visual: A phone screen with the ‘Answers with sources’ lab: a question box (‘When do the exams start?’), bars ranking the school’s documents, and an answer card quoting the exam timetable with ‘Source: Exam timetable’. Then a question about last year’s football match gets ‘I can’t find this… ask the office’. A finger edits a document.
scenes.animation: Bars grow to rank the documents; the quote card slides in; the edited text changes and the answer updates.
scenes.on_screen_text: App lab: take a design apart
scenes.narration: In the app, take apart a finished design: a helper that answers questions about a school. Watch it search the documents, quote the one it used, and say when it doesn’t know. Then edit a document, and see the answer change.

scenes.visual: Dr Farah beside the helper on a phone, which shows a question with an empty search result. Two answer cards appear beside her.
scenes.animation: Cards bounce in one by one.
scenes.narration: Your turn. A student asks something that isn’t in the documents. What should the helper do?

scenes.visual: The ‘Say so, and point to a person’ card gets the check badge, then the screen resolves into the five questions from earlier, with a person standing beside them.
scenes.animation: Points tick in one by one; the takeaway bar rises last.
scenes.on_screen_text: People first · Permission · Plan for harm
scenes.narration: Say so, and point to a person: an honest “I don’t know” beats a confident guess. Remember: start with the problem and its people, and ask if AI is needed. Plan the data, with permission. And plan for harm, so a person stays in charge.

scenes.visual: A student at a kitchen table with one sheet of paper, headed ‘Our AI plan’, filling in boxes: problem, people, is AI needed, data and permission, when it’s wrong. A younger sibling peers over. Dr Farah smiles at the side.
scenes.animation: Each box on the sheet fills with handwriting as it is said; end card fades in.
scenes.narration: Try it yourself: write a one-page plan for an AI that helps your school or community. Name the problem and its people, and say if AI is needed. Then plan the data, and plan for mistakes.

checkpoints.prompt: When you design an AI solution, what should come first?

options.text: A catchy name for the app

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — start from a real problem and the people who have it, then decide whether AI fits at all.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — tools and names come later. Start from a real problem and the people who have it.

checkpoints.prompt: A student asks something that isn’t in the documents. What should the helper do?

options.text: Say so, and point to a person

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — “I don’t know, ask the office” protects people from a confident mistake.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — a confident guess could leave someone stranded. It should say it doesn’t know and point to a person.
